newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cash rates little changed, T-bills sell well.
newsitem.headline: Greek cash rates little changed, T-bills sell well.

text.p: Greek interbank rates were holding morning levels in late quiet trade and dealers said liquidity will be tighter Tuesday on Friday's forex-linked outflows and good T-bill sales today, traders said.

"There was activity in depos and swaps till mid-session but rates held steady around morning levels," said a dealer at a state bank. "Trade is subdued now and T-bill sales must have exceeded maturities by 10 to 20 percent and coupled with Friday's forex outflows will squeeze liquidity tomorrow."
The market was swept by rumours that the finance ministry offered to pay 0.30 percent commissions to some banks that would buy T-bills for their own accounts in excess of 20 billion drachmas.
Commercial banks get a commisssion of 0.45 percent when they buy T-bills for sale to their customers but nothing for own account.
The finance ministry's T-bill issue featured a 10 basis point cut in rates. The 12-month, six-month and three-month T-bills will fall to 12.70 percent, 12.10 percent and 11.90 percent respectively.
T-bill expiries amounted to 580 billion drachmas, traders said.
Early elections are to be held on September 22 but the market has taken a positive attitude towards them on the grounds that the winner will have no option but to follow Greece's EU convergence plan.
The mark was quoted at 159.77/82 drachmas from Monday's 159.635 fix, the dollar at 236.59/69 drachmas from 236.780 and the Ecu at 301.20/30 from 301.200 drachmas.
